Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pdecompR 0.1.0

First release. pdecompR is a finite-element framework for partial differential equations on two-dimensional domains, written in R on top of the sparse matrix classes of ‘Matrix’.

Geometry and meshes

  • Rectangular and simple polygonal domains with validation.
  • Structured triangular meshes and polygon meshes, with checks of connectivity, orientation and degeneracy, quality measures, named boundary markers and named regions (subdomains).
  • Uniform refinement and newest vertex bisection; boundary markers and regions are inherited by refined meshes.
  • Import of Gmsh 2.2 and 4.1 meshes (physical lines become boundary markers, physical surfaces become regions) and export to VTK, including quadratic P2 cells, displacement vectors and stress fields.

Discretization

  • Continuous Lagrange P1 and P2 elements on triangles, scalar and vector valued, with Gaussian quadrature on intervals and triangles.
  • Sparse assembly of stiffness, mass, advection and boundary operators and load vectors.
  • Coefficients given as numbers, functions of (x, y) or (x, y, t), finite-element functions, constant symmetric tensors or piecewise values by region (region_coefficient()).
  • Dirichlet, Neumann and Robin conditions; pure Neumann problems with a compatibility check and a zero-mean gauge.
  • A weak-form language (trial_function(), test_function(), grad(), dot(), integrate_domain(), integrate_boundary()) for linear scalar problems.

Problem classes

  • Elliptic problems with diffusion, advection and reaction, with optional SUPG stabilization.
  • Heat and general linear parabolic problems with backward Euler and Crank-Nicolson (Rannacher startup), time-dependent data and coefficients, and mass diagnostics.
  • Reaction-diffusion systems with IMEX and fully implicit Newton time stepping.
  • Quasilinear diffusion, semilinear reaction and p-Laplace problems solved by damped Newton iteration.
  • Linear elasticity in plane strain and plane stress with displacement, roller and traction conditions, and strain, stress and von Mises output.

Solvers

  • Sparse Cholesky and LU, and preconditioned conjugate gradients, BiCGSTAB and GMRES, with residual and conditioning diagnostics and an explicit status for every solve.

Verification and adaptivity

  • L2, H1 and energy error norms against exact or finite-element reference solutions, and convergence studies with observed orders.
  • Symbolic manufactured solutions through the optional ‘symcompR’ package.
  • A residual a posteriori error estimator, Doerfler marking and an adaptive solve loop.
  • A benchmark suite of ten reference problems in benchmarks/.

Inference and control

  • Discrete forward and adjoint sensitivities of linear elliptic problems.
  • Parameter estimation with adjoint gradients, bounds (including fixed parameters) and Gauss-Newton standard errors.
  • Distributed optimal control with optional control bounds.
